name: selectorToLayerSelector
signature: export function selectorToLayerSelector(selector: Selector, ctx: AbilityContext): LayerSelector
rules: CR 613.6 the set is locked at the moment the effect starts applying
contract: Resolves the DSL selector against the CURRENT board and returns an ids selector holding those concrete ids. It does not translate the filter tree into a LayerMatchFilter.

That is the point. CR 613.6 locks the affected set when a one-shot effect starts applying, so Giant Growth on a bear must keep pumping THAT bear and must not start pumping a creature that arrives later. A translated match filter would re-evaluate on every layer pass and pump the newcomer.
An empty resolution returns the none selector, not the all selector. The failure direction matters: none is a visible no-op, all would pump the whole table.
Ids come back in resolveSelector order, which is seat order, so the list is identical on every client.

evidence.claim: affected objects are pinned rather than re-matched

assertions.given: a target selector naming one bear
assertions.expect: ids kind, exactly that one id

assertions.given: an all-creatures-you-control selector on a board of two
assertions.expect: ids kind with both, in seat order

assertions.given: a creature added to the board after the call
assertions.expect: the returned selector does not include it

unlocks.source: supporting primitive for P01 and P02
